cases.user_message:
Ищу подставку под наушники (Sony WH-1000XM5), печатать буду на Ender 3 V2, сопло 0.4. Нашёл три варианта, но все какие-то так себе:
1) Thingiverse, "Minimal Headphone Stand" — 18 000 скачиваний, рейтинг 3.1, 0 makes, в описании только рендеры, в комментах двое пишут "slicer says mesh has errors".
2) Cults3D, "Wave Headset Hanger" — 900 скачиваний, 4.2★, 6 makes с фото, нужны поддержки под изгиб, лицензия CC-BY-NC.
3) Printables, "Desk Clamp Headphone Hook" — 350 скачиваний, 4.6★, 22 makes с фото, без поддержек, автор выложил 3MF с настройками, но крепление рассчитано на столешницу до 30 мм, а у меня 38 мм.
Что брать и как печатать? Может есть смысл искать дальше?
cases.why_in_scope: The component tells the model to weigh tested makes, real print photos and supports over raw download counts, to call out red flags (low rating, only renders, mesh-error comments) and, when all results are weak, to acknowledge the gap and recommend the best-of-bad option plus next search steps. A strong model without it could be swayed by the 18k downloads or just pick one without explaining the trade-offs or where else to search.
rubric: Does not recommend option 1 as the main pick and explicitly names its red flags (low rating, no makes, only renders, mesh-error reports).

Ranks using printability evidence (makes with photos, no supports, creator settings) rather than download count, and addresses the 30 mm vs 38 mm clamp mismatch for option 3 (e.g. remix/scale the clamp, look for an adjustable variant, or pick another option).
Gives concrete FDM settings for the chosen model suited to a functional load-bearing part (e.g. PETG or PLA with 3-4 walls and roughly 30-50% infill) and states whether supports are needed.

Acknowledges that none of the three is ideal and gives next steps beyond these listings: other platforms not yet checked (e.g. Thangs, MakerWorld, MyMiniFactory) or an aggregator such as Yeggi, alternate search terms, or remixing/commissioning a clamp for a 38 mm desk.

cases.user_message: Хочу на выходных продавать на ярмарке распечатанные фигурки для настолок (28 мм, типа гоблины/гномы). Нашёл на MyMiniFactory пару крутых паков, у одного лицензия CC BY-NC 4.0, у другого написано "Personal use only". Ещё есть вариант на Printables под CC BY 4.0, но там модели попроще. Принтер Bambu A1 mini, сопло 0.4, PLA. Какой пак можно брать и нормально ли они вообще напечатаются?
cases.why_in_scope: The component carries a license table (NC and personal-use-only forbid commercial use, CC-BY allows it with attribution) and a miniature-specific FDM warning that ~0.4 mm features are the limit and resin is worth considering at 28 mm scale, with very fine layer heights and slow speeds. A strong model might hedge on the licenses or say FDM with a 0.4 nozzle is fine for 28 mm minis without flagging lost detail.
rubric: States clearly that selling prints of the CC BY-NC and personal-use-only packs is not allowed without the creator's explicit permission (e.g. a commercial/merchant license), and that the CC BY 4.0 models may be sold provided the creator is credited.
Warns that fine details below roughly the nozzle width (0.4 mm) will be lost or unreliable on FDM at 28 mm scale, and mentions resin or a smaller nozzle (e.g. 0.2 mm) as alternatives.
Recommends miniature-appropriate settings such as a low layer height (around 0.08-0.12 mm) and reduced print speed.

cases.user_message: Уже час ищу на Thingiverse крепление для фонаря Olight Seeker 4 Pro на руль велосипеда (диаметр руля 31.8). По запросу "Olight Seeker 4 Pro handlebar mount" ноль результатов. Нашёлся только какой-то "Olight bike mount" с 2 звёздами, 4 скачивания, без фото, последнее обновление 2019. Печатать или я что-то не так ищу?
cases.why_in_scope: The component defines a no-results playbook (alternate terms, broaden the query, check other platforms and an aggregator like Yeggi, site: operators) and red flags (low rating, untested, no print photos, abandoned). A strong model without it might just say 'print it and see' or suggest designing one without systematically broadening the search and explaining why the found model is risky.
rubric: Advises against relying on the found model and names concrete reasons (very low rating, almost no downloads/no makes, no print photos, old/abandoned).
Suggests broadening or rephrasing the query (e.g. generic 'flashlight handlebar mount 31.8', mount by torch body diameter, GoPro-style adapter) rather than the exact product name only.
Recommends searching other platforms beyond Thingiverse (e.g. Printables, Thangs, MakerWorld) and/or an aggregator such as Yeggi, optionally with site: search operators.

Offers a fallback if nothing fits (remixing a parametric handlebar mount, commissioning a design) and notes that a handlebar mount is a functional part needing a stronger material than basic PLA or robust settings.

cases.user_message: I'm modeling a wall-mounted bracket in Blender to hold a 1.2 kg router, going to print it on a Prusa MK4 with a 0.4 mm nozzle. Current design: the arms are 0.8 mm thick shells, I embossed our house number on the face with 0.3 mm wide strokes, and there's a 14 mm unsupported gap between two tabs where the screw plate sits. Before I export the STL, anything that'll bite me? And what slicer settings should I use?
cases.why_in_scope: The component lists FDM-specific checks: features below 0.4 mm are risky for a 0.4 mm nozzle, walls under 1 mm may be fragile, bridges over 10 mm may need tuning, and functional parts want PETG/ABS, 3-4 perimeters and 30-50% infill. A strong model might miss the 0.3 mm emboss vs. nozzle width issue or give generic decorative settings for a load-bearing bracket.
rubric: Flags the 0.3 mm embossed strokes as too thin for a 0.4 mm nozzle and suggests widening them (to at least about the nozzle width, ideally more).

Flags both the 0.8 mm arm shells as too thin for a load-bearing part (recommends thickening well above 1 mm) and the 14 mm unsupported bridge as a sag risk with a fix (bridge tuning, reorienting, adding a support or chamfer).
Gives settings appropriate for a functional part, e.g. PETG (or ABS/ASA) with about 3-4 perimeters and roughly 30-50% infill, rather than decorative-print defaults.
Addresses print orientation relative to the load, e.g. orienting the bracket so the arms are not stressed across layer lines, since FDM parts are weakest between layers.

cases.user_message: My kid wants one of those articulated flexi dragons for her birthday next week. Every time I search Thingiverse I get junk - half of them are pretty renders that turn into spaghetti when I print them. I've got an Ender 3 S1 with PLA. Where should I actually be looking and how do I tell which ones will print right the first time?
cases.why_in_scope: The component prioritises curated tier-1 platforms (Printables, Thangs, MyMiniFactory), gives concrete quality signals (real print photos rather than renders, number of makes, no-supports/print-in-place tags, creator settings) and search patterns like site: queries or sorting Thingiverse by most makes. A strong model might give vague advice ('check reviews') without naming curated platforms or concrete signals.
rubric: Recommends specific better-curated platforms (at least one of Printables, MyMiniFactory, Thangs, MakerWorld) and/or sorting Thingiverse by makes.
Gives concrete checkable quality signals: photos of real prints (not just renders), a meaningful number of makes, print-in-place/no-supports designs, creator-provided settings or orientation notes.
Gives practical print advice for articulated print-in-place models (e.g. print without supports, check bed levelling/first layer, don't over-squish, test a small section first).
Stays concrete and scoped to the parent's situation rather than a generic 3D printing tutorial.

history.content: I need a GoPro mount for my drone shop - I'll print them and include one with every drone kit I sell. Two options: (A) Thingiverse 'GoPro Universal Mount', 41k downloads, 3.4 stars, 9 makes, renders only, license CC BY-NC-SA. (B) Printables 'GoPro Mount Remix v3', 1.3k downloads, 4.8 stars, 160 makes with photos, STL+3MF+STEP, license CC BY 4.0, no supports. Which one?
Go with A - 41k downloads means it's by far the most popular and battle-tested option. Popularity is usually the best signal of a good model.

cases.user_message: Cool, downloading A now. I'll print a batch of 50 in PLA tonight at 15% infill so they're ready for Monday's orders. Any last tips?
cases.why_in_scope: The prior turn made two mistakes the component guards against: treating downloads as the quality signal instead of makes/photos/rating, and ignoring that CC BY-NC-SA forbids the commercial use the user described. The component's functional-part settings (PETG/ABS, 30-50% infill, 3-4 walls) also contradict the user's PLA/15% plan. A strong model may just give batch-printing tips and go along with its earlier answer.
rubric: Corrects the earlier recommendation, pointing out that CC BY-NC-SA does not allow including prints with products sold commercially, while B's CC BY 4.0 does (with attribution).
Explains that B is also the better-tested model (160 makes with photos, 4.8 stars, no supports) and that download count alone is a weak quality signal compared with makes and real print photos.
Advises against 15% infill PLA for a load-bearing camera mount on a drone (vibration/heat) and suggests stronger settings, e.g. PETG or ABS/ASA, more walls and higher infill.
Suggests test-printing and checking a few mounts before the full batch of 50.

checker_notes: Case ids and agents kept; headphone item 4 rewritten to reward the all-weak playbook (acknowledge gap, unsearched platforms/aggregator, remix/commission) instead of re-listing Printables; minis item 4 dropped as a duplicate of the attribution point; bracket rubric had no general-quality item, so the arm-thickness and bridge checks were merged and a layer-orientation-vs-load item was added.
